newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - DUTCH STOCKS SEEN LIMPING TO YEAR END.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - DUTCH STOCKS SEEN LIMPING TO YEAR END.

text.p: Dutch stocks face a rocky ride to the end of the year and a recovery is expected to be only slight during 1998, a Reuters survey of world stock markets showed on Wednesday.
A survey of Dutch equity analysts on June 11 and 12 showed on average that the AEX index of leading shares was expected to fall more than seven percent from current levels by the end of the year.
Dutch shares were seen as overvalued and predictions for the AEX ranged between 700 and 850, compared with the June 12 close of 839.36.
Such a performance would make the Dutch stock exchange the worst performer among the world's top 15 bourses, according to the Reuters poll.
But the worst should be over by the end of 1997 and 1998 should see steady, if unspectacular, increases, the survey indicated.
Six analysts gave an average end-1998 prediction for the AEX of 883, an improvement on current levels of just over five percent.

"EMU jitters will impact interest rates in the coming 12-15 months. This...will depress the valuation of the Dutch equity market, which is currently extremely overvalued," said ING Barings in a comment on the Dutch market.
"After returning to an average or fair valuation in the second half of 1997, we foresee a slight recovery during next year."
In its end-1997 forecast Delta Lloyd Bank also said the current market was overvalued and a moderate further rise in interest rates was expected.
But on the positive side, the bank said good earnings growth and demand from pension funds would help to consolidate share levels.
